## Overview

Not every model is written with ModelingToolkit. The constructor
`next_generation_matrix(F, V, x₀, p)` accepts van den Driessche and Watmough's `𝓕` and
`𝒱` as ordinary Julia functions of the infected-state vector and differentiates them with
ForwardDiff at the infection-free state. This vignette uses it for an SEIR model with two
kinds of vaccine, *leaky* (every vaccinated person is partially protected) and
*all-or-nothing* (a fraction is fully protected), and compares the closed forms obtained
symbolically.

## Plain functions

```{julia}
using ReproductiveNumbers, LinearAlgebra

# infected states x = (E, I); the uninfected state enters through p
F(x, p) = [p.β * p.S₀ * x[2] / p.N, 0.0]
V(x, p) = [(p.σ + p.μ) * x[1], -p.σ * x[1] + (p.γ + p.μ) * x[2]]
p = (β = 0.5, σ = 0.25, γ = 0.2, μ = 0.01, N = 1000.0, S₀ = 1000.0)
ngm = next_generation_matrix(F, V, zeros(2), p; infected = [:E, :I])
```

```{julia}
basic_reproduction_number(ngm)
```

The sign conventions are checked automatically; a mistake such as putting a transition
into `F` with the wrong sign is reported:

```{julia}
Vbad(x, p) = [-(p.σ + p.μ) * x[1], (p.γ + p.μ) * x[2]]
ngm_bad = next_generation_matrix(F, Vbad, zeros(2), p)
validate_decomposition(ngm_bad)
```

## Leaky versus all-or-nothing vaccination, symbolically

With ModelingToolkit we can compare the two vaccine models in closed form. A fraction `v` of
the population is vaccinated. With an all-or-nothing vaccine of efficacy `ε`, a fraction
`ε v` is fully protected and the rest is fully susceptible. With a leaky vaccine every
vaccinated person has susceptibility reduced by the factor `1 - ε`.

```{julia}
using ModelingToolkit, Symbolics
using ModelingToolkit: t_nounits as t, D_nounits as D

@parameters β σ γ μ N v ε
@variables S(t) Sᵥ(t) E(t) I(t) R(t)
λ = β * I / N
# all-or-nothing: the protected fraction never enters the model's susceptible pool
aon = complete(System(
    [D(S) ~ -λ * S, D(E) ~ λ * S - σ * E, D(I) ~ σ * E - γ * I, D(R) ~ γ * I],
    t; name = :aon))
ngm_aon = next_generation_matrix(
    aon, [E, I]; equilibrium = Dict(S => (1 - ε * v) * N, R => 0))
R_aon = basic_reproduction_number(ngm_aon)
```

```{julia}
# leaky: vaccinated susceptibles Sᵥ are infected at rate (1 - ε) λ
leaky = complete(System(
    [D(S) ~ -λ * S, D(Sᵥ) ~ -(1 - ε) * λ * Sᵥ,
        D(E) ~ λ * S + (1 - ε) * λ * Sᵥ - σ * E,
        D(I) ~ σ * E - γ * I, D(R) ~ γ * I],
    t;
    name = :leaky))
ngm_leaky = next_generation_matrix(
    leaky, [E, I]; equilibrium = Dict(S => (1 - v) * N, Sᵥ => v * N, R => 0))
R_leaky = basic_reproduction_number(ngm_leaky)
```

Both reduce `R₀` by the same factor `1 - ε v`:

```{julia}
symbolic_isequal(R_aon, R_leaky)
```

so the critical vaccination coverage is `v* = (1 - 1/R₀)/ε` for both:

```{julia}
R0 = β / γ
vstar = (1 - 1 / R0) / ε
symbolic_isequal(substitute(R_aon, Dict(v => vstar)), 1)
```

The two vaccines differ in the *endemic* equilibrium and in the final size, not in the
threshold; those differences appear once the vaccinated class is depleted differently, which
is a question about the non-linear model rather than about `R₀`.

## Sensitivity of the critical coverage

```{julia}
sensitivities(vstar, [β, γ, ε])
```
